key_moments.description: Ahasuerus held a great feast in Shushan the palace. On its seventh day, when he was merry with wine, he sent for Queen Vashti to show off her beauty, but she refused, and he burned with anger.
key_moments.title: Defied by Queen Vashti

key_moments.description: The king loved Esther more than all the other women and put the royal crown on her head in place of Vashti. Then he held a great feast for his princes and servants, called Esther's feast.
key_moments.title: Crowns Esther Queen

key_moments.description: Haman told the king of a people whose laws were different and offered silver to have them destroyed. The king gave Haman his ring and let him deal with the people as he liked.
key_moments.title: Gives Haman His Ring

key_moments.description: One night the king could not sleep, so he had the records read to him. He heard how Mordecai had exposed a plot to kill him, and learned that nothing had been done to honor him.
key_moments.title: Hears How Mordecai Saved Him

key_moments.description: When Esther pleaded for her life and her people, the king asked who had dared to do this. She named Haman, and the king had him hanged on the gallows he had built for Mordecai.
key_moments.title: Has Haman Hanged

name: Xerxes
summary: A king who reigned over 127 provinces, from India to Ethiopia, from his throne in Shushan the palace. He put away Queen Vashti, made Esther his queen, and turned against Haman when Esther revealed his plot.

key_moments.description: After the angel's promise to Zacharias, Elisabeth became pregnant and stayed hidden for five months. She said the Lord had taken away her shame among people.
key_moments.title: Conceives in Her Old Age

key_moments.description: When Mary greeted her, the baby leaped inside Elisabeth and the Holy Ghost filled her. She called Mary blessed among women and the mother of her Lord.
key_moments.title: Feels Her Baby Leap at Mary's Greeting

key_moments.description: Elisabeth gave birth to a son, and her neighbours rejoiced with her. When they wanted to name him after his father, she said he would be called John.
key_moments.title: Naming Her Son John

name: Elizabeth
summary: A woman descended from Aaron, married to the priest Zacharias, who had no children into old age. God gave her a son, John, and when Mary visited, she was filled with the Holy Ghost and blessed her.

key_moments.description: While Zacharias burned incense in the temple, an angel appeared beside the altar. The angel told him his prayer was heard and Elisabeth would bear him a son named John.
key_moments.title: Visited by an Angel at the Altar

key_moments.description: Zacharias asked how he could know this, since he and his wife were old. Gabriel said that because he did not believe, he would not be able to speak until it happened, and he came out unable to talk.
key_moments.title: Struck Dumb for Not Believing

key_moments.description: When the baby was eight days old, Zacharias asked for a writing tablet and wrote that his name was John. At once he could speak again, and he praised God.
key_moments.title: Writing the Name John

key_moments.description: Filled with the Holy Ghost, Zacharias blessed God for coming to save His people. He said his son would be called the prophet of the Highest and go before the Lord to prepare His ways.
key_moments.title: Zacharias Prophesies

name: Zechariah
summary: A priest who, with his wife Elisabeth, had no children into old age. The angel Gabriel told him he would have a son, John, and because he did not believe, he could not speak until the boy was named.

key_moments.description: While Queen Vashti held a women's feast, the king, merry with wine, sent for her to come wearing the royal crown so the people could see her beauty. Vashti would not come, and the king burned with anger.
key_moments.title: Refuses to Come to the King

key_moments.description: Memucan said Vashti had wronged not only the king but all the people, for wives everywhere would look down on their husbands. So a royal law was given that Vashti must never again appear before the king, and her place would go to another.
key_moments.title: Removed as Queen

name: Vashti
summary: Vashti was the queen of King Ahasuerus. When she would not come at his command, the king took away her royal place and later made Esther queen instead.

key_moments.description: Elisabeth gave birth to a son in her old age. Neighbours wanted to name him after his father, but she said he would be called John, and Zacharias wrote the same.
key_moments.title: Named John

key_moments.description: John preached in the wilderness of Judaea, telling people to repent because heaven's kingdom was near. He wore camel's hair, ate locusts and honey from the wild, and baptized people in the Jordan.
key_moments.title: Preaches in the Wilderness

key_moments.description: Jesus came to be baptized, and John said he needed to be baptized by Jesus instead. When Jesus came up from the water, the Spirit came down like a dove and a voice from heaven spoke.
key_moments.title: Baptizing Jesus

key_moments.description: Seeing Jesus coming toward him, John called Him the Lamb of God who takes away the world's sin. The next day two of John's disciples heard him and followed Jesus.
key_moments.title: Calls Jesus the Lamb of God

key_moments.description: John told Herod it was not lawful for him to have his brother's wife, so Herod put him in prison. At Herod's birthday feast, the daughter of Herodias asked for John's head, and Herod had him beheaded.
key_moments.title: Beheaded by Herod

name: John
summary: The son of Zacharias and Elisabeth, sent by God to prepare the way for Jesus. He preached repentance, baptized people in the Jordan, and pointed others to Jesus as the Lamb of God.

key_moments.description: When Esther's turn came to go to the king, she won the favor of all who saw her. The king loved her more than all the other women and put the royal crown on her head in place of Vashti.
key_moments.title: Made Queen

key_moments.description: Esther asked all the Jews in Shushan to fast for her three days and nights, and said she and her maidens would fast too. Then she would go in to the king, against the law, even if it cost her life.
key_moments.title: Calls a Three-Day Fast

key_moments.description: Three days later Esther stood in the king's inner court, and he held out his golden sceptre to her. She invited the king and Haman to a banquet she had prepared.
key_moments.title: Goes In to the King

key_moments.description: At her next banquet Esther asked the king for her life and the lives of her people, who had been sold to be destroyed. When the king asked who had done this, she said it was this wicked Haman.
key_moments.title: Names Haman as the Enemy

key_moments.description: Queen Esther and Mordecai wrote with full authority to confirm the days of Purim. Esther's decree settled these matters, and it was recorded.
key_moments.title: Confirms the Days of Purim

name: Esther
summary: Esther was a Jewish orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai who became queen to King Ahasuerus. She risked her life to go before the king and saved her people from Haman's plot to destroy them.

key_moments.description: The Jewish elders built and did well as Haggai and Zechariah prophesied. They finished God's house in King Darius's sixth year.
key_moments.title: Prophesies as the Temple Is Built

key_moments.description: The LORD gave Zechariah a message for the people. The LORD said that if they turned to Him, He would turn to them, and told them not to be like their fathers who would not listen.
key_moments.title: Calls the People to Turn Back

key_moments.description: One night Zechariah saw a man on a red horse standing among myrtle trees, with red, speckled and white horses behind him. They had been sent by the LORD to walk through the earth, and they found it still and at rest.
key_moments.title: Sees Horses Among the Myrtles

key_moments.description: The LORD told Zechariah what He wanted from His people. They were to judge truly, show mercy to one another, and not oppress widows, orphans, strangers or the poor.
key_moments.title: Calls for Justice and Mercy

name: Zechariah
summary: A prophet, the son of Berechiah, who spoke to the people who had come back to Jerusalem. With Haggai he urged them to build the house of God, and the LORD showed him visions in the night.

key_moments.description: As Mordecai sat at the king's gate, he learned that two of the king's doorkeepers planned to kill King Ahasuerus. He told Esther, she told the king in Mordecai's name, and the matter was recorded in the king's chronicles.
key_moments.title: Saving the King's Life

key_moments.description: The king's servants bowed to Haman as the king had commanded, but Mordecai would not. He had told them he was Jewish, and Haman, full of anger, set out to destroy all of Mordecai's people.
key_moments.title: Refuses to Bow to Haman

key_moments.description: Mordecai warned Esther that she would be no safer in the palace than the other Jews. He asked who knew whether she had become queen for this very time.
key_moments.title: Tells Esther Not to Keep Silent

key_moments.description: The king told Haman to dress Mordecai in royal clothes and lead him on the king's horse. So Haman brought him through the city, crying out that this was how the king honored a man.
key_moments.title: Honored Through the City

key_moments.description: After Haman was hanged, the king gave Mordecai the ring taken back from Haman. Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's house.
key_moments.title: Given the King's Ring

name: Mordecai
summary: Mordecai was a Jew of the tribe of Benjamin in Shushan who raised his cousin Esther as his own daughter. He would not bow to Haman, urged Esther to plead for her people, and rose to be next to the king.

key_moments.description: The angel Gabriel told Mary she had found favour with God and would bear a son named Jesus. She asked how this could be, then called herself the Lord's handmaid and agreed.
key_moments.title: Told She Will Bear Jesus

key_moments.description: Mary hurried to see her cousin Elisabeth, and Elisabeth's baby leaped at her greeting. Mary praised the Lord and stayed about three months.
key_moments.title: Visiting Elisabeth

key_moments.description: In Bethlehem Mary gave birth to her firstborn son and placed Him in a manger. When the shepherds came, she treasured all of this and thought it over in her heart.
key_moments.title: Gives Birth to Jesus in Bethlehem

key_moments.description: Mary stood near the cross of Jesus. Seeing her and the disciple He loved, Jesus gave them to each other as mother and son.
key_moments.title: Stands at the Cross

key_moments.description: After Jesus was taken up, Mary the mother of Jesus prayed together with the apostles, the women and His brothers in Jerusalem.
key_moments.title: Praying With the Disciples

name: Mary
summary: A virgin of Nazareth, engaged to Joseph, whom the angel Gabriel told she would bear the Son of God. She gave birth to Jesus in Bethlehem and stood by His cross.

key_moments.description: King Ahasuerus set Haman over all his princes, and the king's servants bowed to him. When Mordecai would not bow, Haman was full of anger and planned to wipe out all the Jews in the kingdom.
key_moments.title: Furious at Mordecai

key_moments.description: Lots were cast before Haman to choose a day, and he persuaded the king to let a people be destroyed. Letters sealed with the royal ring were sent to every province to kill every Jew on one day.
key_moments.title: Wins a Decree to Destroy the Jews

key_moments.description: Haman went home glad after Esther's banquet, but the sight of Mordecai at the gate spoiled it all. His wife Zeresh and his friends told him to build a tall gallows to hang Mordecai on, and he had it made.
key_moments.title: Has Gallows Built for Mordecai

key_moments.description: Haman thought the king wanted to honor him and described a royal parade. Then the king told him to do it all for Mordecai, and Haman went home mourning with his head covered.
key_moments.title: Leading Mordecai's Horse

key_moments.description: When Esther named Haman as her enemy, he was afraid and begged her for his life. The king had him hanged on the gallows he had built for Mordecai.
key_moments.title: Hanged on His Own Gallows

name: Haman
summary: Haman the Agagite was raised by King Ahasuerus over all the princes. Furious that Mordecai would not bow to him, he plotted to wipe out all the Jews, but he was hanged on the gallows he had built for Mordecai.
